headline: Profit rebounds, cash flow swings negative post spin-off

drivers.explanation: Growth of 7% in North America and 7% in South America, partially offset by a 7% decline in EMEA; adjusted for FX/commodities, revenue rose just 1%.
Prior-year quarter carried a ~$300M tax valuation-allowance charge tied to OECD Pillar Two guidance; Q1 2026 tax expense was $81M vs $356M a year earlier.
Release attributes margin compression to increased commodity costs and unfavorable foreign currency exchange, partially offset by increased volumes.
Flat y/y because cost of sales grew about as fast (+6.7%) as revenue (+5.4%), netting to no change in gross profit dollars.
Reflects $1,577M of proceeds from new senior and junior note issuances in the quarter, ahead of using Versigent spin-off distribution proceeds to redeem $1,847M of notes in April.
Reflects the same new senior and junior notes issued in Q1, prior to the April redemption of $1,847M of notes funded by Versigent spin-off proceeds.
Quarter reshaped by the April 1 spin-off of EDS as Versigent; CEO Kevin Clark cited a "sharper focus" and "strong free cash flow generation enabling incremental value creation."

summary_short: Aptiv posted Q1 2026 revenue of $5,086M (+5% y/y) and swung to $189M net income from a $11M loss a year earlier, while operating cash flow fell to -$143M from $273M as the EDS spin-off reshaped the balance sheet.
summary_long: Revenue rose 5% y/y to $5,086M (just 1% adjusted for FX/commodities), on 7% growth in North America and South America offsetting a 7% EMEA decline. Net income swung to $189M from a $11M loss, mainly because Q1 2025 carried a ~$300M tax valuation-allowance charge; diluted EPS moved to $0.88 from -$0.05. Adjusted EBITDA margin compressed to 14.8% from 15.7% on higher commodity costs and unfavorable FX. Operating cash flow fell to -$143M and free cash flow to -$362M on working-capital use. The EDS business spun off as Versigent on April 1; new guidance is issued for 'New Aptiv' ex-EDS: FY2026 revenue $12.8-13.2B, Adjusted EBITDA $2.36-2.48B.
